title: Unified Onramp Migration Strategy to Redwood API - parity & console checklist
summary: Redwood AE/SE run a parity-focused migration demo for Arboretum Labs that currently runs a mixed fleet on OpenAI+Anthropic+Together. Core themes: matching latency and output parity, routing and fallbacks, VPC/private deployment options, KMS and audit log requirements. Agreed next step: schedule two-week pilot with cost/latency benchmarks and send security pack + pilot agreement.
topics: parity mapping (tokens, output shape, stop sequences)
dedicated vs hosted economics and SLOs
Optimize recommendations: batching, KV cache, quantization
action_items: Alex Nguyen - Send pricing worksheet and pilot agreement by 2026-10-20
Priya Shah - Share benchmark template and sample postman collection by 2026-10-19
Sanjay Rao - Provide current traffic profile and 95th p95 latency targets by 2026-10-22
next_steps: Run parity benchmark comparing two models (openai-gpt-like, anthropic-chat-like) to Redwood-vendor candidates
Customer to grant test tokens and a small dedicated VLAN for pilot
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Marisol Vega (Arboretum CTO), Derek Chu (ML Eng), Sanjay Rao (Infra Lead), Alyssa Kim (PM)

[00:00] Alex Nguyen: hey everyone thanks for joining on a sunday, appreciate it. this is alex from redwood, with priya and marcus, we'll walk through a migration parity map and console ops. can everyone quick intro?
[00:32] Marisol Vega: marisol here, arboretum labs. we've got a mixed setup right now, openai for chat, anthropic for higher safety, together for some tuned models. want to consolidate and control costs.
[01:15] Priya Shah: thanks marisol, quick clarifying q: are you aiming for a full cutover or staged canary approach?
[01:40] Marisol Vega: staged — want canaries, traffic split. also compliance, SOC two and VPC for some data flows.
[02:10] Derek Chu: we also have inference caching upstream; we rely on prefix cache and a KV cache in our infra, want to make sure k-v cache behavior maps.
[02:45] Marcus Lee: noted. on the redwood side we have automatic prefix/KV caching, and you can pin model versions per route. we'll show the console.
[03:20] Alex Nguyen: high-level agenda: demo API parity mapping, console tour for routing/rollouts, optimize recommendations, and then security + next steps.
[04:05] Priya Shah: first, parity. for tokens and response shape, folks often see small diffs: stop sequence handling, chunking, and metadata fields. we have an adapter pattern in our SDK to normalize responses from openai/anthropic/together to a consistent schema.
[05:00] Derek Chu: curious: how do you handle function calling differences? together and anthropic have slightly different event shapes.
[05:28] Priya Shah: great q — we map function-calls at the SDK layer and the API supports structured output. we showed an example in the deck, basically a transform step that preserves original call semantics. sometimes transcription will show 'functioncall' vs 'fn call' — little noise.
[06:10] Marisol Vega: latency is key. our p95 for chat is about 220ms now; cost is second. if switching increases p95 by >50ms it's hard to sell.
[06:40] Alex Nguyen: understood. we have benchmarked candidates that hit 180-250ms p95 depending on sequence length and hardware. with Redwood Dedicated you can lock SLOs and get predictable p95. for hosted, we have traffic shaping and region routing to keep latency low.
[07:25] Marcus Lee: also KV cache — for completions with repeated prefixes, effective latency can be ~50ms lower because of cached key/value hits. we can show logs.
[08:00] Alyssa Kim: can we get a demo of the console rollout flows? we need canary, auto-fallback if rollout fails, and route-level cost tracking.
[08:30] Priya Shah: sure — switching to screen share, walking through console. (screen noise) so here is a route "chat-frontend-prod", we pin model versions per route, set traffic weights, and create a canary with 5% traffic for 24 hours. you can set fallback rules to a cheaper variant or different region.
[09:40] Marisol Vega: is there per-token cost broken down by route and model?
[10:00] Marcus Lee: yes, token-level cost and latency breakdown by key/route/model. you can query the console for cost per million tokens per model; we also emit telemetry for per-request token counts.
[10:35] Derek Chu: security — we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. plus data residency in eu-west for certain customers.
[11:00] Alex Nguyen: all supported. we have enterprise packages: SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit logs retention, and KMS/HSM integration. for private deployments we can do VPC peering or on-prem air-gapped bundles. we'll attach the security pack after.
[11:35] Marisol Vega: do you have SOC two and iso certs?
[11:45] Priya Shah: SOC 2 Type II in our security pack; ISO is in progress. we'll share certs.
[12:20] Alex Nguyen: switching back to parity mapping, here's a concrete example: openai's stop token semantics sometimes produce a trailing whitespace, anthropic has guardrails that truncate earlier. we provide tokenizer-agnostic post-processing rules to match behavior across models during the pilot so your front-end sees consistent outputs.
[13:20] Derek Chu: that post-processing — is it client side or in redwood?
[13:35] Priya Shah: typically in the SDK layer customers run it client-side; for Private deployments we can also put a transform lambda in the control plane.
[14:00] Marisol Vega: what about function response latency at scale? some of our calls hit many tokens.
[14:25] Marcus Lee: for long contexts we recommend chunked streaming and kv cache to reuse attended tokens. also quantization on dedicated hardware reduces GPU memory pressure and improves throughput.
[15:10] Alex Nguyen: let me show a quick cost example: for a high-frequency chat route with avg 120 tokens per response, using batching and a quantized candidate reduces cost by ~30% in our examples vs the unoptimized baseline on other vendors.
[15:50] Derek Chu: can we see the benchmark template?
[16:05] Priya Shah: yes, we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and a postman collection. it includes p50/p95/p99 latency, token counts, and a tokenized parity score to measure textual differences.
[16:40] Alyssa Kim: how do rollbacks work? if a canary exhibits higher hallucination rate?
[16:55] Priya Shah: console will auto-roll back by policy if error or quality regressions exceed thresholds; you can also hook an automated eval that runs sample prompts through both variants and fails when a regression is detected.
[17:35] Marisol Vega: auditors will want immutable logs for who changed routing and when.
[17:50] Marcus Lee: audit logs capture route changes, user, timestamp, and old/new config. retention is configurable per plan.
[18:20] Derek Chu: we also need to test warm start times for KV cache after pod restarts.
[18:40] Priya Shah: we instrument KV cache warmups; typical warm start impact is a one-off spike, but with autoscaling and pre-warm hooks you can avoid user impact. we'll include measured cold-start graphs in the pilot report.
[19:10] Alex Nguyen: switching to private/dedicated options: Dedicated gives reserved capacity, lower jitter. Private gives VPC and KMS control. which are you leaning toward?
[19:35] Marisol Vega: for regulated workloads we need private in eu-west for some customers, but we'd like to pilot hosted first for dev and early prod.
[20:00] Alex Nguyen: common approach: hosted pilot -> dedicated reserved for prod APIs that need SLOs -> private for regulated partitions.
[20:30] Derek Chu: what's typical timeline for a pilot? we have a lot of traffic but can carve off small percentage.
[20:50] Priya Shah: we recommend two weeks with baseline + a set of workload tests; enough to gather token-level telemetry, stability, and early cost signals.
[21:20] Alex Nguyen: demo time — quick API parity example. (screen) here is a request to redwood's /v1/generate endpoint, same request body structure as openai but with model: "rwd-chat-large-1"; note stop sequences and function call fields are supported.
[22:10] Marisol Vega: so we don't have to rewrite callers much?
[22:20] Marcus Lee: minimal changes — mostly endpoint swap and a thin adapter for metrics and structured outputs. for function-calls we showed how to map signatures.
[23:00] Derek Chu: error codes mapping? openai returns 429s with different headers.
[23:20] Priya Shah: we normalize rate-limit headers and surface consistent retry-after and quota info. fallback routing helps redirect to cheaper variants when throttled.
[24:00] Marisol Vega: ok demo looks good. can you show the Optimize suggestions for our traffic profile?
[24:20] Priya Shah: yes — Optimize analyzes sequence length distribution and recommends batching window, token limit per request, and quantization profile; it also suggests model family swaps for cost/latency tradeoffs. for your traffic profile (you said avg 120 tokens, many short messages) it recommends dynamic batching at 30ms and a medium quantization profile for models that support it.
[25:10] Derek Chu: what about evals for hallucination? we have domain-specific prompts.
[25:30] Marcus Lee: you can upload prompt sets and run continuous evals; the platform will surface regression alerts tied to those prompts.
[26:00] Marisol Vega: on the pilot, what telemetry do you need from us?
[26:12] Alex Nguyen: tokenized prompt/response samples (anonymized if needed), traffic split config, and a list of top 200 prompt templates used. that helps create parity tests.
[26:45] Alyssa Kim: data retention concerns: we want short-term logs for pilot but not store PII — can you redact?
[27:05] Priya Shah: yes, redaction rules at ingest, and you control retention per route. we'll document defaults.
[27:40] Derek Chu: any gotchas moving from together? we rely on some ensemble models.
[27:55] Marcus Lee: ensembles are supported by doing routing policies that fan-out to several model variants and then a lightweight ranker; there is an extra cost but it's doable.
[28:30] Alex Nguyen: quick pause — questions?
[28:40] Marisol Vega: you mentioned cost per million tokens — can we see example math with our traffic?
[29:00] Marcus Lee: sure — if you do 100M tokens / month on a mid-tier model, estimated hosted cost with optimization is X, vs dedicated commit of Y which amortizes to Z per token; we'll send a tailored worksheet.
[29:40] Derek Chu: how do we measure parity automatically?
[29:55] Priya Shah: benchmark template calculates BLEU-like text diffs and an acceptance threshold for important templates; it also computes token-level divergence metrics.
[30:25] Alyssa Kim: are there limits on concurrent streams?
[30:40] Marcus Lee: concurrency depends on the plan; with Dedicated you get predictable pool sizing. for hosted we have soft limits and can offer burst capacity.
[31:10] Marisol Vega: we need auditability on model versions for regulators.
[31:25] Alex Nguyen: every request includes model version metadata and we persist mapping for audits; rollouts are also versioned.
[31:55] Derek Chu: can we do a smoke run with 1% traffic mirrored? we want to compare outputs without impacting users.
[32:10] Priya Shah: yes — traffic mirroring is supported; you can mirror 1% to the pilot stack and run comparisons.
[32:45] Marisol Vega: perfect. let's talk integration checklist — what do we need to do for an initial pilot?
[33:00] Alex Nguyen: checklist: 1) grant dev/test API tokens, 2) provide sample prompts and traffic profile, 3) select two candidate models to test, 4) agree pilot window and SLA we measure, 5) sign a short pilot agreement.
[33:45] Alyssa Kim: timeline for privileged credentials?
[33:55] Alex Nguyen: we can issue temporary dev credentials within 24 hours once NDA/pilot agreement signed.
[34:20] Derek Chu: are there any compatibility shims for tool calling? we use custom tool endpoints.
[34:35] Marcus Lee: yes, tool bindings are configurable; our SDK maps tools to HTTP endpoints with retries and timeouts.
[35:00] Marisol Vega: any expected migration risks?
[35:15] Priya Shah: main risks: slight output drift, initial latency jitter, and infra cold starts; mitigations: canary, traffic mirroring, caching warmups, and tweak quantization.
[35:45] Alex Nguyen: show an example pilot report (screen). includes p50/p95/p99, token cost delta, parity score, and regression flags.
[36:15] Marisol Vega: can we include customer-specific prompt sets in the regression detection?
[36:30] Priya Shah: yes, you provide labeled prompts and expected answers; the platform flags deviations.
[37:00] Derek Chu: on encryption, does redwood support customer-managed keys?
[37:12] Marcus Lee: yes KMS support and HSM for Private deployments.
[37:40] Marisol Vega: do we need to change our infra for VPC peering?
[37:55] Alex Nguyen: minimal changes — network whitelisting and a peering config. our infra team supports setup.
[38:25] Alyssa Kim: follow-up: can you run a small benchmark with our top-10 prompts and return a pilot report?
[38:40] Priya Shah: yes, that's part of the pilot scope. we'll need the prompts and expected outputs.
[39:05] Derek Chu: curious about multi-region failover and routing policy granularity.
[39:20] Marcus Lee: routing policies can target region, model variant, and customer tier; automatic failover to another region is supported with cross-region caching considerations.
[39:55] Marisol Vega: are there per-route quotas and rate limiting?
[40:10] Alex Nguyen: yes per-route quotas, token quotas, and rate limits with retry headers surfaced.
[40:40] Derek Chu: about observability, can we stream logs to our splunk/kinesis?
[40:55] Priya Shah: yes we support event export to SIEMs and cloud sinks; PII redaction is configurable.
[41:25] Marisol Vega: ok real question: can you guarantee no higher hallucination rate?
[41:40] Priya Shah: we cannot guarantee zero change; we guarantee to measure and provide rollback/fallbacks. the eval suite helps detect regressions quickly.
[42:10] Alex Nguyen: let's recap decisions: pilot window ~two weeks, mirror 1% traffic, run top-10 prompt benchmark, and share security docs.
[42:40] Marisol Vega: agreed. we'll prepare the prompt set and traffic sample.
[43:05] Alex Nguyen: action items we'll capture: send pricing, send security pack, send benchmark template, issue dev tokens after pilot agreement.
[43:30] Derek Chu: one more technical — how do you handle streaming chunk ordering? sometimes tokens arrive shuffled with other vendors.
[43:50] Marcus Lee: streaming is ordered, we have seq ids and chunk checks. if a mismatch happens we drop and re-request chunk.
[44:20] Alyssa Kim: any limit on eval upload size?
[44:35] Priya Shah: reasonable limits, but we can take larger uploads for enterprise pilots via S3 transfer.
[44:55] Marisol Vega: cost: what's the delta to keep both vendors during pilot?
[45:10] Alex Nguyen: you can mirror at low percentage and only pay for pilot compute — we bill pilot usage separately and we can cap spend. we'll include numbers in the pricing worksheet.
[45:40] Derek Chu: regarding model versions, do you keep older weights accessible for audits?
[45:55] Marcus Lee: snapshots of model mappings and configs are retained; weights depend on model licensing but we keep version metadata.
[46:25] Marisol Vega: ok good. any regulatory concerns for eu data?
[46:40] Priya Shah: we can host Private control plane in eu-west and ensure data egress rules; KMS in-region is supported.
[47:05] Alex Nguyen: last demo bit — console's cost explorer and anomaly detector. (screen) it highlights token spikes and suggests batching changes.
[47:40] Alyssa Kim: great. can you share the recording and a short write-up?
[47:50] Alex Nguyen: yes recording and summary, plus the security pack and pilot paperwork.
[48:10] Marisol Vega: timeline: we'll review internally and aim to sign pilot agree by 10-22.
[48:35] Derek Chu: pledge to send top-10 prompts and traffic profile by 10-20.
[49:00] Alex Nguyen: we'll prepare the pricing worksheet and dev credentials once the paperwork is done.
[49:25] Priya Shah: any other technical blockers?
[49:35] Sanjay Rao: just network approvals for peering — our infra team will coordinate.
[49:50] Alex Nguyen: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[50:05] Marisol Vega: thanks folks, appreciate the demo.
[50:25] Marcus Lee: thanks all. bye.
[50:40] (call ends, recording stops)
notes: Customer specifically asked for 1% traffic mirroring and top-10 prompt benchmarks. Security emphasis: SOC2, SAML, KMS, EU data residency. Agreed pilot approach: hosted pilot with potential later Private/Dedicated for regulated subsets.
